findings.title: Radar Visibility & Feedback
findings.where: Arena and Road screens, bottom left corner panel
findings.problem: The radar is a solid black disc with a barely visible, low-contrast cyan sweep wedge. There are no contact dots visible for enemies or objectives.
findings.why: It reads as a broken instrument or a missing asset rather than a functional tool. Players rely on it for situational awareness; a black disc provides zero information and causes anxiety about whether the game is working.
findings.fix: Fill the radar background with a very faint, dark grey grid or range rings to give it scale. Make the sweep a semi-transparent, brighter green/white wedge. Add distinct, high-contrast red dots for enemies and green dots for objectives to ensure they pop against the dark background.

findings.title: Speedometer Secondary Information Legibility
findings.where: Arena and Road screens, bottom center panel
findings.problem: The '0 mph' text is massive and white, but critical stats like 'TIER 2/3' and '0.0 mi' are tiny, grey, and have low contrast against the dark panel background.
findings.why: Players need to know their tier (difficulty/power) and mileage (progress) at a glance. The current hierarchy prioritizes speed (which is good) but makes the secondary info illegible at a glance, requiring the player to squint or focus hard to understand their status.
findings.fix: Increase the size and font weight of the 'TIER' text. Use the game's accent color (teal or bright green) for the Mileage ('0.0 mi') to make it distinct from the grey text. Ensure the '100%' status indicator is brighter.

findings.title: Player Visibility and Map Clutter
findings.problem: The player car (orange rectangle) blends into the background noise. Several buildings (top right, middle right) have yellow/orange roofs or awnings that compete with the car's color. The massive circular wall is also visually loud and distracts from the player.
findings.why: In a city, orienting the player is crucial. If the player blends in or competes with environmental geometry, navigation becomes stressful and confusing, breaking the flow of the game.
findings.fix: Add a distinct, bright outline (cyan or white) to the player car to separate it from the buildings. Reduce the opacity or saturation of non-interactive background buildings slightly to create depth and push them back. Make the 'Up' arrow above the car larger, brighter, and perhaps pulsing.

findings.title: Abstract Car Blueprint Visualization
findings.problem: The car diagram labeled 'SUBCOMPACT - TOP VIEW' is just a blue rounded rectangle with a dotted line. It doesn't resemble a vehicle or reflect the specific parts (body/chassis) selected on the left.
findings.why: It disconnects the player from their creation. It looks like a placeholder graphic. Players need to see *what* they are building to feel a sense of progress and ownership.
findings.fix: Render a recognizable top-down vehicle silhouette (wheels, distinct body shape, maybe a turret) inside the bounding box. Ensure the silhouette changes shape or complexity based on the selected 'Body' and 'Chassis' stats (e.g., a 'Heavy' chassis should result in a boxier, larger silhouette).

findings.title: Inconsistent UI Aesthetics (Title Menu)
findings.problem: The menu box ('1 New Driver') is a flat rectangle with a thin blue outline. It looks like a standard HTML input field or a basic window frame, clashing with the heavy, industrial/terminal aesthetic of the in-game UI (like the Condition panel).
findings.why: It breaks immersion immediately upon starting. It feels 'webly' or like a browser extension rather than a cohesive game interface. It lacks the 'weight' or 'terminal' aesthetic established in the gameplay screens.
findings.fix: Style the menu box to match the in-game HUD: dark background, perhaps a subtle scanline texture, distinct colored borders (green/teal) for the active selection, and a monospaced font. Make it look like a CRT terminal interface to match the game's vibe.
